title: Ashura: Husayn at Karbala
hookLine: Shia Muslims mourn the martyrdom of Husayn, the Prophet's grandson, at Karbala in 680, and many Sunnis grieve him too

cards: In parts of Iraq, Iran, Lebanon, Pakistan, India and far beyond, on the tenth of Muharram, streets fill with people dressed in black. Some walk in long processions.
Some sit in halls listening to a reciter tell a story they already know by heart, and weep anyway.

And along the roads, people hand out water, free, to anyone who passes: cups of it, jugs of it, stands built just for the day. The water is part of the story. Today, the same date as yesterday, and a different memory.

teach.b: Husayn ibn 'Ali was the grandson of the Prophet ﷺ, the son of his daughter Fatima and of 'Ali. Hadith collections record the Prophet's deep love for him. In Tirmidhi, he says Husayn is from me and I am from Husayn.
In the year 680, Yazid, son of Mu'awiya, had become ruler and demanded the allegiance of the leading Muslims. Husayn refused to give it.
He set out toward Kufa in Iraq, where people had written urging him to come, with his family and a small band of companions.

teach.h: KARBALA, CUT OFF FROM THE RIVER.
teach.b: At Karbala, near the Euphrates, a much larger army surrounded them and cut them off from the river. For days the camp went without water, children included.
On the tenth of Muharram, Husayn and nearly all the men with him were killed.
The women and children, among them his sister Zaynab, and his son 'Ali, who had been too ill to fight, were taken captive to Kufa and then to Damascus.
The sources tell that Zaynab spoke out boldly before the governor and before Yazid himself.

For Shia Muslims, Karbala is at the heart of their faith and history. 'Ashura is a day of mourning, majalis gatherings, recitations and processions, a remembering that keeps the question alive: what does it mean to stand against injustice when it costs everything?
Many Sunni Muslims grieve Husayn deeply too, and honor him as a member of the Prophet's family; they understand some of the events and their meaning differently, and mark the day differently.
The grief for a grandson killed beside a river he wasn't allowed to drink from is shared widely. That's why there's water on the roads.

how: Shia Muslims observe the first ten days of Muharram with mourning gatherings (majalis), recitations of the Karbala story, processions and free water stands (sabil); many Sunni Muslims also remember Husayn on 'Ashura, often alongside fasting.

games.q: it's the year 680. the new ruler, Yazid, demands Husayn's pledge of allegiance. what does Husayn do?
o: give the pledge and stay safely in Medina.
refuse, and set out with your family toward Kufa.
flee to a distant land and stay silent.
games.why: he refused, and set out with family and a small band of companions. at Karbala, on the tenth of Muharram, he was killed.

practice: Picture a family in the heat with no water, and a river just out of reach, and stay with that for a moment. Then think of who near you could use water: a delivery driver, a coworker on a long shift, a stranger in the sun.
If you pray, you can remember Husayn and his family.

wordCard.voice: 'Ashura again, the tenth of Muharram. For Shia Muslims above all, the day Husayn, the Prophet's grandson, was killed at Karbala. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Karbala, the place in Iraq where Husayn was killed in 680; today a city and shrine.

carryVoice: Your line: he stood for justice. The week ran from walking humbly and the firm middle, through deeds turned to good, a close, a new year, and two 'Ashuras. See you tomorrow.
